literal.prompt: Как называют первые рыхлые кристаллы, возникающие в морской воде до образования сплошной корки?

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: L84 identifies first small needle-like frazil crystals in freezing ocean water; they precede accumulation and bonding into a sheet. Russian ледяные иглы is a descriptive rendering of those needle-like marine crystals in this explicit water context, not an asserted WMO-certified Russian translation. L85 nilas is already continuous; L88 pancakes are accumulated disks with raised edges; L171/L194/L228 fastice is a fixed coastal ice mass. Only key3 matches initial loose crystals before continuous crust.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Это ледяные иглы. При начале замерзания морской воды они всплывают, скапливаются и соединяются в ледяной покров.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: L84 explicitly says frazil crystals float to surface, accumulate and bond into sheets as seawater begins to freeze. L85-L91 adds calm/rough-water routes; short explanation does not claim immediate sheet formation without intermediate stages or identical conditions everywhere. Marine initial-crystal context prevents confusion with atmospheric ice needles.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Нилас — тонкая сплошная корка морского льда.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: L85 explicitly defines nilas as continuous thin ice sheet. This own-option fact accurately explains why nilas fails the before-continuous-crust condition; label is a real marine ice stage.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Блинчатый лёд состоит из круглых льдин с приподнятыми краями, сталкивающихся на волнах.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: L88 defines circular pancake disks with raised rims caused by ocean waves bumping them together. Concrete own-option morphology/mechanism and credible neighbouring form; not unbound frazil or fastice fact.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Припай — морской лёд, неподвижно прикреплённый к берегу или дну.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: L171 directly defines fast ice anchored to shore or ocean bottom; L194 and complete continuationL228 confirm pinned coastal ice without free drift. Own note says shore OR bottom, not necessarily both. It is not the initial loose suspended stage.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Ледяные иглы почти не содержат соли: растущие кристаллы вытесняют её в окружающую воду.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: L84 explicitly says growing frazil crystals expel salt and consist of nearly pure fresh water. L116-L117 independently distinguish saline liquid brine droplets trapped BETWEEN ice crystals from the unsalted crystals themselves; bulk new sea ice can be salty. Note refers to needles/crystals, not whole new ice or liquid pockets, so nearly-salt-free is accurate and qualified.
